cards.text: Here's a Psalm of David, written for the choirmaster and set according to Jeduthun, one of the musicians chosen to give thanks to the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:41). This one's a song, friend. David starts by telling us where his soul goes to rest.

cards.question: David says his soul finds rest in God and in his own strength.

cards.text: God alone is his rock, his salvation and his fortress. That's not one lock on the door, friend, that's THREE deadbolts.

cards.question: With God as his rock and his fortress, what does David say about himself?

answers.text: He will never lose a battle

cards.text: Then David speaks to the people threatening a man: "How long will you threaten a man?" I bet this has been going on a while.

cards.question: David asks if they'll all throw that man down. What does David picture the man as?

cards.text: Their whole plan is to cast him down from his lofty perch. And they delight in lies.

cards.question: These people are two-faced. With their mouths they ___, but inwardly they ___.

cards.text: That's the coworker who says "Love it!" in the meeting and then rips it APART in the group chat, friend. Then comes a Selah, and David tells his own soul to rest in God alone, because his hope comes from Him.
Then that line comes back: God alone is his rock, his salvation and his fortress, and David will not be shaken. And now his salvation and his honor rest on God, his strong rock.

cards.question: Now David turns to everybody listening, "O people" and he tells them to trust God at ___ times.
David tells the people to keep their hearts to themselves and stay quiet before God.

cards.text: Then he says it plain: "God is our refuge." And next, David sizes people up: "Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie."

cards.question: Weighed on a scale, what happens to these men, lowborn and exalted alike?

cards.text: Put them all together and they're still just a vapor, like the steam off my oven door: there, then GONE. Then David gives a warning: "Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods."

cards.question: David says that if your riches increase, you should set your heart upon them.

cards.text: Then David says God has spoken once, and he has heard it twice. ONCE, friend, and my oven timer has to ding NINE times before I hear it one time.

cards.question: God has spoken once, and David heard it twice. What did David hear?

cards.text: Then David turns and speaks right to God: loving devotion belongs to You, O Lord. Power AND loving devotion, friend, both from the same God.

cards.question: Power belongs to God, and loving devotion belongs to the Lord too. Then David ends with this: God will ___ each man according to his ___.

findings.problem: David appears for the first time only in the phrase "A Psalm of David." The card never says simply who he is, such as David, Israel's king.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question depends on "they" and "that man" from the preceding story card. On its own, it does not identify the people who are threatening the man, so it lacks the required context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "These people" points back to people identified on an earlier card. The question should identify them itself as the people intending to cast the man down.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The earlier cards do not set up the time extent of David's call to trust God. The blank therefore asks for the unseen wording "all" rather than testing a meaning the baker has been equipped to reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card repeats that power belongs to God, which comes from Psalm 62:11, but cites only Psalm 62:12. Its citation is too narrow for the verses it uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The preceding story card sets up power and loving devotion but gives no context from which to reason out repayment or deeds. Both blanks ask for the unheard wording of the final line rather than an inferable meaning.
